title: Carry an authoritative producer-lifecycle invocation identity from command start to end, so a fresh same-key check is distinguished from a repeated ACP frame of an older unfinished one
outcome: The host can tell, from evidence carried through the real command start and end, whether a later command start under the same check key is a genuinely fresh invocation or a repeated observation (for example a repeated ACP frame) of an older unfinished one. A fresh independently started check keeps its own credit; an old Unknown or unfinished original stays uncredited and cannot be resurrected; no transcript-id-alone, later-grant, later-turn or old-run-terminality signal is treated as a new-invocation certificate.
acceptance: Each supported command producer identifies its authoritative creation/dispatch and matching end/abandonment boundary in a source-backed design; repeated ACP frames, missing identities, command-text fallbacks, replay and reconnect limitations are explicit. No local ordinal, transcript id, current host turn/grant or old run terminality alone certifies a new invocation.

The same producer-owned invocation identity and producing runtime are carried through recorder forwarding, original launch capture, delayed descriptions, asynchronous/off-lock work, completion and abandonment to the existing observation/check owners. An end without a proven start creates no start, binding, grant, source basis or credit; delayed old callbacks cannot select a newer same-key invocation.

Scope qualification: The supported live-stream assumption is that a producer creation denotes a new invocation unless it matches identity proof still retained by the existing owners. Loading/history frames and callbacks identified as belonging to a prior invocation do not create a new start. Once a completed invocation has released its slot and all facts distinguishing its identity have been lost, an unmarked replay of its creation and completion may be admitted as a new invocation and may receive NEW verification credit if the current start independently satisfies binding, grant, claim, source and result rules. The host does not guarantee detection of that case. It must not recover the old invocation's authority, change its recorded result, or settle any still-owned old check through the newly admitted reference. Known replay/proof loss is not permission to rebind an existing old reference. This limitation creates neither a permanent admission cutoff nor a new identity-history store.

Additional owner-loss qualification: When the existing producer correlation owner and its distinguishing state are irrecoverably lost, resume/load does not by itself prohibit NEW creation admission. The host cannot determine whether a previously observed invocation completed, remained unresolved, or was refused during capacity overflow. An unmarked replay may therefore be admitted under current start/authority/source/result rules and receive NEW verification credit in any of those cases; this residual risk is accepted. A surviving owner retains its known overflow latch and original references across wrapper or reader recreation; a freed slot, host turn or new grant never clears that surviving latch. Loss of the owner is not proof of a genuinely fresh native scope. History/known-old callbacks and end-only events still create no start; no old authority or result is recovered or modified, and a new reference cannot settle a still-owned old check.

A genuinely distinct invocation under a reused legacy key can receive its own valid bound/granted start and checkpoint verification without upgrading the older invocation's authority or result. An older check already closed Unknown stays uncredited. An older legitimately unfinished current/carried check may settle only through its own existing start, authority, source and receipt rules; the new invocation neither grants nor removes that eligibility. Repeated observations of the older invocation cannot acquire later authority. The original fresh-rerun Some(1) positive, ordinary writer/bookkeeping behavior and real current/carried receipt behavior remain intact.

Invocation correlation neither grants authority nor supplies a successful result: original binding/grant/source facts, existing command/result qualification, writer exclusions and current/carried transfer guards remain independent. Unknown, NotFinished, artifact settlement, abandonment and retained history do not become positive execution proof. Description changes and duplicate terminal events remain attributable to their exact invocation without changing another invocation's facts.

Invocation proof stays bounded and process-local in the existing producer/recorder/observation owners; eviction, runtime replacement, replay, reconnect or reload cannot reconstruct lost proof from durable rows or treat an old frame as fresh. Loss or saturation has an explicit affected identity/producer scope, visible non-qualifying behavior and a source-backed recovery boundary; it does not invalidate unrelated still-proven invocations or existing properly owned carried checks. No parallel history registry, new durable schema or public raw provider identity is introduced without a separately concurred design amendment.

Producer-faithful ordinary regression coverage retains the fresh same-key positive and existing replay negatives, and covers the second genuine ACP call, changed descriptions, late old end after new start, duplicate terminal, missing identity, runtime replacement/proof loss, and actual typed/legacy/current/carried forwarding. Fixture representation changes preserve all credited/no-credit/invalidation assertions and have explicit independent concurrence. Exact-input required checks, full gate and independent cross-vendor review must pass before acceptance/landing; source analysis alone is not execution evidence.
